q: What is the empirical scaling of the minimum braid-word approximation error epsilon_min(L) for Hadamard and T under Fibonacci braiding, and does it match the Solovay-Kitaev prediction epsilon ~ 2^(-c L^(1/alpha)) with alpha = log_2(5)?
basis: Our BFS gives only two data points (Hadamard at L=13 -> 0.029, T at L=14 -> 0.032). The wave brief calls for reproducing the density claim numerically; the natural next step is to characterise the density RATE, not just its existence at a single depth.
next_steps: Run BFS to depths L = 4, 6, 8, ..., 20 (with meet-in-the-middle to keep memory tractable). Fit log(epsilon_min) vs L and vs L^(1/alpha) to see which functional form describes the envelope. Compare against the Solovay-Kitaev bound and against Freedman-Larsen-Wang's explicit polylog(1/eps) claim.

q: How does the numerical density rate compare across Fibonacci (SU(2)_3), Ising (SU(2)_2), and metaplectic (SU(2)_4) anyons at matched braid length? Ising is famously not universal (Clifford only) -- is this visible as a plateau in epsilon_min(L)?
basis: Our replication only builds Fibonacci. But the paper's whole architecture is about which SU(2)_k are universal. A comparative BFS across the three most-studied cases would surface the qualitative difference between universal and non-universal anyons empirically, not just theoretically.
next_steps: Extend fibonacci_anyons.py to a template that takes the F- and R-symbols of any modular tensor category. Build the (F,R) for Ising (well-known: R = e^(+/- i pi/8) on the sigma-sigma-psi vertex) and SU(2)_4. Run identical BFS on each; plot epsilon_min(L) side by side and confirm the Ising plateau at Clifford-group distance.

q: The paper's 2-qubit gate construction uses B_6 on 6 anyons in V^0(6) + V^2(6). What is the shortest braid word that approximates CNOT within epsilon = 10^-2, and how controllable is the leakage out of the 4-dimensional computational subspace?
basis: We only implemented the 1-qubit computational subspace (3 anyons, dim 2). The paper's core algorithmic step is the 2-qubit gate; that is where 'leakage error' first appears (paper Section 2) and it is the load-bearing part of the polynomial-equivalence argument.
next_steps: Implement V^0(D_ij, 6 pts) direct sum V^2(D_ij, 6 pts) with the corresponding B_6 action. Encode CNOT in a 4-dim computational subspace of the 5-dim total space. Run BFS + optionally a leakage-penalised optimiser (e.g. gradient descent on braid parameters). Report both the fidelity to CNOT and the fraction of amplitude that leaks outside the computational subspace as a function of L.

q: Our density search deduplicates by rounding the SU(2)-mod-phase matrix entries to 4 decimal places. This gives a coarse lattice cover but may collapse near-degenerate distinct group elements. Would a hyperbolic-geometry-aware nearest-neighbour index (using the Fubini-Study metric on SU(2)/U(1) ~ S^2) find shorter braid approximations?
basis: During the run we observed the search-frontier size grow roughly like c^L (c~2) rather than 4^L, showing significant collision. Whether those collisions are true equalities (relations in B_3) or lattice artefacts of the 1e-4 rounding is not clear from our current instrumentation.
next_steps: Replace the coarse hash with a ball-tree over SU(2)/U(1) using the great-circle distance. Compare (i) frontier growth rate, (ii) best epsilon at fixed depth. If the true group image at level 5 is a dense subgroup, the growth rate under an exact metric should stay exponential.

q: Freedman-Larsen-Wang work at r=5 (Fibonacci); Freedman-Kitaev-Wang extend density to r >= 5, r != 6. Is the density-search efficiency (accessible distinct group elements per depth L) monotone in r, or does it peak at some intermediate value?
basis: The paper explicitly picks r=5 as the smallest universal level. Practical topological quantum computing proposals also target Fibonacci because of gate-compilation efficiency. But it is not obvious whether higher r gives 'more room' (bigger Lie group -> more elements accessible per step) or 'more decoherence-of-search' (more sparsely populated group).
next_steps: Instantiate SU(2)_r for r in {5, 7, 9, 11} on the 3-anyon computational subspace (dimension grows with r). Run BFS at matched braid depth L and record the size of the reachable set + best distance to Hadamard. Report as a heatmap: (r, L) -> epsilon_min. Discuss implications for anyon-hardware level-selection.
